rulings.challenge_claim: observed_substrate_signals affirmatively states "no tov-opener... token in this span," but 7:18 itself opens with tov and is one of the strategy's own seven ch-7 tov-opener sites, left completely undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Byte-confirmed: oshb:Eccl.7.18 opens with tov (“ט֚וֹב אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֶּאֱחֹ֣ז בָּזֶ֔ה”, byte tier), and the staged tov_openers inventory lists it as the 7th of 7 in-chapter sites (7:1, 7:2, 7:3, 7:5, 7:8, 7:11, 7:18; 12 book-wide). observed_substrate_signals' claim of ‘no tov-opener ... token in this span’ is byte-false for the span's own closing verse. The admonition_unit call plausibly survives despite the omission: 7:18's own construction (tov + relative clause governing a deictic pronoun, “ט֚וֹב אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֶּאֱחֹ֣ז בָּזֶ֔ה”) differs from the nominal tov-X-min-Y comparative form of the other six ch.7 tov-openers, and its own “וְגַם מִזֶּ֖ה אַל תַּנַּ֣ח אֶת יָדֶ֑ךָ”/“ט֚וֹב אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֶּאֱחֹ֣ז בָּזֶ֔ה” deictic pair (‘this’/‘that’) depends on the two prohibitions just stated in 7:16-7:17 — so 7:18 cannot stand alone as a free member of the sentence zone's tov-comparative series even though it is nominally inside that inventory. The defect is non-disclosure, not a boundary error.
rulings.remedy: See the combined remedy under the OL ruling for this row (same cure applies to both items).

rulings.challenge_claim: Two stated grounds are refuted by the row's own closing verse: it declares no tov-opener or refrain token in the span when its last verse IS a tov-opener, and it claims the unit resolves on a positive imperative when that verse carries a third negative imperative it declines to quote.
rulings.grounds: All five points confirmed. (1) Convergent with the LF item: 7:18 is byte-confirmed as the 7th of 7 ch.7 tov-opener sites, undisclosed. (2) The row's byte-tier quote of 7:18 stops before “וְגַם מִזֶּ֖ה אַל תַּנַּ֣ח אֶת יָדֶ֑ךָ” — a third אל-plus-jussive negation (matching the pattern of 7:16's אל תהי/ואל תתחכם and 7:17's אל תרשע/ואל תהי), omitted from the row's quoted run. (3) The row's claim that the counsel ‘resolves on a positive imperative’ has no byte referent anywhere in the verse: the quoted closing clause “כִּֽי יְרֵ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים יֵצֵ֥א אֶת כֻּלָּֽם” has “יְרֵ֥א” (‘one who fears’) as a substantive adjective functioning as the SUBJECT of “יֵצֵ֥א”, a 3rd-person imperfect/future verb (‘will come out’) — there is no imperative or jussive verb anywhere in this clause; the row's own WEB gloss (‘he who fears God will come out of them all’) is itself a gnomic future statement, not a command, and does not support the ‘positive imperative’ characterization either. (4) Undisclosed: 7:18 is this chapter's ONLY ירא (fear-root) site — a skeleton sweep returns exactly 8 verses book-wide (3:14, 5:6, 7:18, 8:12, 8:13, 9:2, 12:5, 12:13), only one of them in ch.7. (5) Undisclosed: “אֱלֹהִ֖ים” is one of only 7 bare (non-definite) Elohim verses against 28 definite (ha-elohim) — the staged inventory confirms 7:18 in the 7-verse bare set, distinct from the two definite ha-elohim forms two rows earlier at 7:13-7:14. (6) The middle verse 7:17 (“אַל תִּרְשַׁ֥ע הַרְבֵּ֖ה וְאַל תְּהִ֣י סָכָ֑ל לָ֥מָּה תָמ֖וּת בְּלֹ֥א עִתֶּֽךָ”) carries NO quoted Hebrew anywhere in the row although the row's ‘two negative imperatives’ claim is itself a Hebrew-form claim resting on only one quoted verse (7:16) plus an English paraphrase of 7:17.
rulings.remedy: (1) Disclose 7:18's tov-opener status (7th of 7 ch.7 sites) rather than asserting its absence, with the construction-difference argument above as the reason it still closes this admonition_unit rather than opening a new tov-series single_saying. (2) Correct ‘resolves on a positive imperative’ to accurately describe the verse's actual grammatical arc: a third אל-plus-jussive prohibition (“וְגַם מִזֶּ֖ה אַל תַּנַּ֣ח אֶת יָדֶ֑ךָ”) followed by a gnomic 3rd-person-future grounding clause (“כִּֽי יְרֵ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים יֵצֵ֥א אֶת כֻּלָּֽם”), not an imperative resolution. (3) Extend the quoted Hebrew run of 7:18 through “וְגַם מִזֶּ֖ה אַל תַּנַּ֣ח אֶת יָדֶ֑ךָ” so the third negation is visible, and add a byte-tier Hebrew quote for 7:17 to support the ‘two negative imperatives’ claim with an actual quoted form rather than only a WEB paraphrase. (4) Optionally disclose the fear-root exclusivity and bare-Elohim form as texture at this seam. Test the cure must pass: a grammatical-form check of any ‘resolves on X’ claim must match an actual verb form quoted at byte tier from the verse itself, and the tov-opener inventory must be disclosed, not denied, for every span-closing verse.

rulings.challenge_claim: The deviation is licensed on a form claim the bytes refute -- the verse does not carry the form-marker of the sayings zone it is being assimilated to -- and the no-shared-token claim survives only under a token-level standard the cluster abandons elsewhere.
rulings.grounds: Both points confirmed. (1) The row licenses its single_saying deviation on the ground that 7:19 is ‘of the same form as the sentence-zone sayings just before it’; that zone's own byte-marker is a verse-initial tov (12 openers book-wide, 7 in ch.7: 7:1, 7:2, 7:3, 7:5, 7:8, 7:11, 7:18). oshb:Eccl.7.19 opens “הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה”, and a chapter-scoped tov-family skeleton sweep (any tov token anywhere in the word, not just openers) returns exactly 11 ch.7 verses — 7:1, 7:2, 7:3, 7:5, 7:8, 7:10, 7:11, 7:14, 7:18, 7:20, 7:26 — with 7:19 confirmed absent from that list. The verse also carries no tov token at all, so the deviation's stated form-match is byte-false. Its comparative is verbal (“לֶחָכָ֑ם מֵֽעֲשָׂרָה֙...”, a finite verb governing a מן-comparative complement) rather than the nominal tov-X-מן-Y construction of the zone's actual sayings (e.g. 7:1's tov-שם-משמן pattern) — a distinct construction the row's ‘same form’ claim conflates with the zone's marker. (2) ‘Shares no content token with the moderation counsel before it’ holds only at strict token identity: under the root-level standard this cluster applies elsewhere as binding cohesion evidence, the חכם (wise) root IS shared — “תִּתְחַכַּ֖ם” (7:16) against “הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה”/“לֶחָכָ֑ם” (7:19), both members of the same final-mem חכם family (16 book-wide) — and 7:19 sits inside the chapter's own wisdom-root chain (medial/final-mem combined family, 7 ch.7 verses: 7:4, 7:10, 7:11, 7:12, 7:19, 7:23, 7:25), which resumes at 7:23 and 7:25 just past this row's closing seam.
rulings.remedy: Rewrite the deviation-license sentence to name the actual warrant — 7:19 is a self-contained VERBAL numeric comparison lacking an observation-frame or narrative marker, distinct in GENRE (aphoristic, non-narrative) though not in FORM from the tov-comparative sayings — rather than claiming an identical construction. Disclose the חכם-root link to 7:16 and the forward chain to 7:23/7:25 as texture, explicitly not treated as merge-grade cohesion since 7:19 carries no grammatical dependency on either neighbor (unlike 7:12's dependency on 7:11). Test the cure must pass: the revised warrant must cite a construction or marker actually present in 7:19's own bytes, not the zone's tov-marker, and must not assert a token-level absence where a root-level sweep this cluster elsewhere treats as binding shows presence.

rulings.challenge_claim: the corollary argument rests on a below-byte-tier particle and an unquoted hinge verse, and the span's opening particle is treated opposite to the way the same cluster treats it two rows earlier.
rulings.grounds: Confirmed. Re-collating the row's own cited particle, spliced byte-for-byte from the row (“גַּם”), against oshb:Eccl.7.21 returns tier=accent_stripped, not byte (source form “גַּ֤ם”) — and 7:21, the corollary's hinge verse, carries NO byte-tier Hebrew quote anywhere in the row (the row's only formatted Hebrew quotes are for 7:20 and 7:22; the full verse “גַּ֤ם לְכָל הַדְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְדַבֵּ֔רוּ אַל תִּתֵּ֖ן לִבֶּ֑ךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא תִשְׁמַ֥ע אֶֽת עַבְדְּךָ֖ מְקַלְלֶֽךָ” is otherwise unquoted). A גם-family skeleton sweep confirms the particle carries no seam-exclusive force in ch.7: 5 verses (7:6, 7:14, 7:18, 7:21, 7:22), none seam-aligned, with 2 tokens inside the row's own closing verse 7:22. Independently confirmed: “צַדִּ֖יק” (7:20) is the 3rd of exactly 3 ch.7 צדיק sites (7:15, 7:16, 7:20), the first two inside earlier rows of this same cluster — undisclosed. The כי-consistency point is directionally correct (the row names no discriminator) but the two uses are not actually contradictory: the row's own opening “כִּ֣י” (7:20) and p02-019's cited “כִּ֛י” (7:12, itself only accent_stripped tier there, per the r1 ruling on that row) are rendered differently by the WEB witness — causally (‘For wisdom is a defense...’, explaining 7:11) at 7:12 versus asseveratively (‘Surely there is not a righteous man...’, opening a new claim) at 7:20 — a real, witness-visible distinction the row could cite rather than a genuine contradiction in the cluster's own evidentiary standard.
rulings.remedy: (1) Re-splice 7:21's opening particle at byte tier (“גַּ֤ם”) with an inline oshb: ref and explicit tier label, and add a byte-tier Hebrew quote for 7:21 itself so the corollary's hinge verse has a quoted anchor. (2) Disclose the צדיק recurrence at 7:15/7:16 as texture. (3) Add one sentence naming the discriminator between this span's opening כי (asseverative, per WEB ‘Surely’) and 7:12's כי (causal, per WEB ‘For’), closing the apparent inconsistency the challenge raises. Test the cure must pass: re-run the collator on the revised 7:21 field and confirm tier=byte.
